# HP5082_7433 - Three-digit seven-segment red LED display, one common cathode per digit

Package DIP-12 · family HP5082 · catalogue file [catalog/chips/HP5082_7433.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/HP5082_7433.json)

## Pins

| Pin | Name | Role | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CATHODE1 | analog | cathode of digit 1 (common to its segments) |
| 2 | ANODEE | analog | anode of segment e, shared by all three digits |
| 3 | ANODED | analog | anode of segment d, shared by all three digits |
| 4 | CATHODE2 | analog | cathode of digit 2 |
| 5 | ANODEC | analog | anode of segment c, shared by all three digits |
| 6 | ANODEDP | analog | anode of segment dp, shared by all three digits |
| 7 | CATHODE3 | analog | cathode of digit 3 |
| 8 | ANODEB | analog | anode of segment b, shared by all three digits |
| 9 | ANODEG | analog | anode of segment g, shared by all three digits |
| 10 | ANODEA | analog | anode of segment a, shared by all three digits |
| 11 | ANODEF | analog | anode of segment f, shared by all three digits |
| 12 | NC | nc | leave unconnected (note 1) |

## Functions

| Output pin | What it does |
|---|---|
| none | A segment lights when current flows from its anode pin into the cathode pin of a digit. The segment anodes of all digits are joined inside (an 8 by 3 array), so the digits are lit one at a time (strobed) (page 81). |

## Electrical

| Value | Figure |
|---|---|
| inputSchmitt | no |
| notes | Per segment: peak forward current 50 mA (pulse under 500 us), average 5 mA max; forward voltage 1.55 typ / 2.0 max V at 5 mA; reverse voltage 5 V max; 80 mW per digit. Peak currents under 3.5 mA are not recommended. Luminous intensity 10 min / 40 typ ucd at 500 uA average, 5 mA peak, 10% duty. Peak wavelength 655 nm (page 79). |

## Notes

Light rise and fall time 10 ns typ (10%-90% of light for a step in current, page 79). On the card SIFF2~, SIFF1~, SIFF0~ drive cathodes 1, 2, 3 (pins 1, 4, 7).

## Sources

- [HP 5082-7430 series Solid State Numeric Indicator (7 segment monolithic), technical data April 1977, in HP 1977 Optoelectronics Designers Catalog](http://www.bitsavers.org/components/hp/1977_Optoelectronics_Designers_Catalog.pdf) - 78-81 (PDF pages 85-88); 5082-7433
